title: The Collapse of College Math Readiness
author: AI Learn Insights
summary: AI Learn Insights uses a UCSD Senate-Administration Workgroup report to document a dramatic collapse in incoming students' math readiness. Until recently, fewer than 1% of entering UCSD students required remedial math; by Fall 2025, nearly 12% -- 921 students -- did, a nearly thirtyfold increase. More alarming, roughly 70% of that remedial group needs help not with high school math but with elementary and middle school foundations. The author names this phenomenon the 'Backward Slide' and traces its downstream effects: students placed into foundational remediation complete STEM-adjacent course sequences at rates three times lower than the baseline, and virtually no student who places into Math 2 at UCSD has ever completed an engineering degree. The essay argues that if gaps are this visible at a highly selective campus, they are likely far worse at regional colleges and community colleges. AI is not the cause of the crisis but will likely deepen it through cognitive offloading -- students bypassing the practice through which mathematical fluency is built.
points: * UCSD remedial math placements rose from 32 students (FA20) to 921 (FA25), a nearly 30x increase, with ~70% of remedial students needing elementary/middle-school-level foundational math. * Students placed into Math 2 (foundational remediation) have a DFW rate of 24-41% across the STEM-adjacent sequence; virtually none complete an engineering degree. * The author hypothesizes that the problem is likely worse at less-selective institutions -- regional four-year colleges and community colleges -- where open access is part of the mission. * AI did not cause the Backward Slide (which coincides with COVID-19) but will worsen the next stage through cognitive offloading: students bypassing math practice by delegating to AI tools. * The essay calls for honest problem-statement discipline before solution-seeking: 'What evidence do you have that your solution solves this math problem? And please, no hand-waving with vacuous terms such as personalization, adaptive learning, or AI-powered tutoring.'
quotes: Until recently, less than 1% (under 50) of incoming students needed remedial math... Today, nearly 12% of entering students (921) require remedial math. That's nearly a thirtyfold increase.
I will call this phenomenon the Backward Slide in math readiness: remediation is moving backward, from college preparation to high-school preparation, and now to middle-school foundations.
In the STEM pathway, the report's conclusion is starker: 'Few, if any students who place into Math 2 have successfully completed an engineering degree.'
My working hypothesis is that the problem is likely worse at less selective institutions, including regional four-year colleges and community colleges.
A danger is cheating, but more consequential is cognitive offloading. Students are increasingly using AI tools to bypass the very practice through which mathematical fluency is built.
UCSD has made the problem visible. Now we need to know how far it extends.
What evidence do you have that your solution solves this math problem? And please, no hand-waving with vacuous terms such as 'personalization,' 'adaptive learning,' or 'AI-powered tutoring.'
